title: Renewal Stabilization Sprint Canvas
body:
Purpose / context:
This is a lightweight, repeatable canvas for running a short "stabilization sprint" when a renewal enters a high-risk zone (score >= 7). The goal: contain risk quickly, create a clear mitigation path, and buy time for product/engineering/customer to remediate while reducing likelihood of churn. Use this when account has 30–90 days to renewal and signals point to possible non-renewal (usage drop, executive disengagement, technical blocker, procurement stall).

Quick summary (one-liner):
- 7-day stabilization sprint to triage, mitigate, and create an exec-ready mitigation plan for high-risk renewals.

When to launch:
- Renewal within 90 days AND account risk score >= 7 OR
- Major outage impacting production SLAs OR
- Executive asks to pause renewal OR
- Repeated quality/regression alerts tied to model outputs

Outcomes by Day 7:
- Prioritized remediation list with owners and SLAs
- A one-page exec brief ready for CRO and account execs
- Temp commitments (support hours, enablement sessions, limited concessions) agreed with CS leadership
- Open engineering/ops tickets with clear priority and ETA or fallback plan

Triage rubric (use to quickly score and prioritize tasks):
- Impact (0–3): 0=no impact, 1=minor, 2=moderate, 3=major production impact
- Visibility (0–2): 0=internal only, 1=account execs aware, 2=customer execs & legal engaged
- Likelihood to block renewal (0–3): 0=unlikely, 1=possible, 2=probable, 3=almost certain
- Time to remediate (0–2): 0=<3 days, 1=3–14 days, 2=>14 days
- Commercial sensitivity (0–2): 0=low, 1=medium, 2=high (contract or SLA risk)
Total score scale: 0–12. Trigger sprint at >=7.

Roles & responsibilities (RACI-style bullets):
- CS Lead (owner): triage convener, customer communication owner, tracks actions.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): diagnose technical causes, produce runbook and patch suggestions.
- Product/PM: assesses product roadmap constraints, approves behavioral/feature workarounds.
- Eng on-call / SRE: timebox hotfix work, updates on ETA and rollback plans.
- Finance/Commercial: evaluates concession proposals and signs off on discounts or credits.
- Executive sponsor: engages if the account demands C-level conversation; approves escalations.

Warroom cadence (recommended):
- Day 0: kick call (30m) - align on problem statement, scope, and triage owners
- Daily standups (15m) - status, blockers, next actions
- Engineering sync (ad-hoc) - as needed for deep debugging
- Day 3 checkpoint (30m) - present patch options, provisional concessions
- Day 7 exec brief (30m) - final mitigation plan and proposed commercial package

Ticketing naming convention and artifacts:
- Prefix all tickets "SPRINT-<account>-<short>" (e.g., SPRINT-acme-model-drift)
- Attach: customer repro steps, sample failing inputs, logs, timestamps, route ID, API request ids
- Add tag: renewal-risk:high and link CS-<account>-renewal in ticket

Stabilization play types (pick 1–3 per sprint):
1) Technical hotfix — patch or soft-fail to restore SLA (short-lived; eng-led)
2) Configuration / routing change — shift traffic to fallback model variant or dedicated pool
3) Usage enablement — 1:1 workshop, prompts tuning, prompt guardrails applied
4) Data hygiene / retraining — quick retrain or negative sample injection (if feasible)
5) Commercial concession — credits, short-term discount, extended support hours
6) Exec engagement — sponsor intro, customer-CEO note, joint roadmap alignment

Decision matrix for choosing plays:
- If Impact=3 and TimeToRemediate>14 => combine Exec + Commercial + Config fallback
- If Impact=2 and TimeToRemediate<=3 => Technical hotfix + Enablement
- If Visibility=2 => always notify Exec sponsor and prepare a one-pager

Communication templates (copy/paste and adapt):
- Slack to internal warroom: "WARROOM START: SPRINT-acme model drift. CS Lead @Samira. SE @Ethan investigating. Kick in 15m in #cs-renewal-warroom. Goal: triage & containment today. TLDR: production error rate up 28% since 11/01."

- Customer-facing acknowledgement (first touch):
Subject: "We’re on it — stabilization plan for <product> issues"
Hi <Customer-AM/Primary>,
Thanks for flagging this — we’ve stood up a stabilization sprint and priority team. Short plan: 1) Contain impact with fallback routing (ETA 4h), 2) Root-cause triage (SE+SRE), 3) Exec brief if needed by Day 3. I’ll be your single point of contact: Samira Patel, samira@redwood.ai.
Quick ask: can you share a recent failing example and approximate traffic window?
Thanks,
Samira

- Exec brief subject line: "[Action required] Stabilization proposal for <Account> — renewal at risk"
One-pager structure (use as slide or doc):
1) Situation summary (concise)
2) Impact metrics (tokens, error rate, revenue at risk)
3) Proposed mitigations (with owners & ETA)
4) Ask from our Exec (sponsor ask / approval of concession)
5) Next steps & timeline

Metrics and dashboards to surface (minimal set):
- Daily active keys and token consumption trend (7d/30d)
- Error rate / failed calls per route (1h, 24h)
- Latency P95 for the account-specific routes (1h, 24h)
- Model output quality regressions (human eval pass/fail)
- Support ticket volume and CSAT for the account
- Contract value at risk (ARR near-term + churn probability)

Commercial guardrails (principles):
- Prefer time-limited concessions tied to technical remediation milestones.
- No discount > 20% without Director approval.
- Credits for downtime should be calculated per SLA clauses, not ad-hoc.

Sample concession template (finance-ready):
- Offer: 10% credit for month X + 2 weeks of priority support (100 hours) if we meet containment milestones A+B by Day 7.
- Approval path: CS Lead -> Sales Director -> Finance (email trail required).

Operational checklist (Day-by-day):
- Day 0: Kick, create SPRINT ticket, notify warroom, send customer acknowledgement
- Day 1: SE validates repro, initial workaround applied, initial ETA for fix
- Day 2: Engineering deep dive, decide patch vs config fallback
- Day 3: Customer update + provisional concession offer if needed
- Day 4–6: Implement patch/config, run smoke tests, internal QA
- Day 7: Exec brief, finalize concession, plan handoff to renewal/AE

Handoff and documentation (post-sprint):
- Convert SPRINT tickets into standard JIRA epic if remediation extends >14 days
- Produce a 1-page postmortem with root cause, mitigations, timeline, and lessons learned
- Update account renewal plan in CRM with new forecast and notes

Retrospective prompts (for continuous improvement):
- What was the earliest signal we missed?
- Were engineers able to reproduce quickly? If not, why?
- Which plays bought the most time? Which did not help?
- What changes to monitoring or runbooks are needed?

Quick templates / checkboxes for the canvas (paste into warroom doc):
- [ ] SPRINT ticket created and linked to renewal record
- [ ] Customer acknowledgement sent
- [ ] Daily standups scheduled (calendar invite + owner)
- [ ] Samples & logs attached to ticket
- [ ] Engineering ETA committed and recorded
- [ ] Concession proposal drafted
- [ ] Exec brief ready by Day 7
- [ ] Postmortem plan assigned

Notes / open questions (working ideas):
- Consider a small pool of discretionary "stabilization credits" that CS Director can approve immediately (under $5k equivalent) to speed response.
- Runbook for automated fallback routing needs a safety checklist to avoid cascading failures.
- Evaluate whether we should cap the number of live stabilization sprints per SRE rotation.

Attachments & examples to add to this doc before finalizing:
- Example SPRINT ticket (template)
- Exec brief example (slide)
- Customer email thread example with approved concession language
- Confluence page link to the renewal scoring algorithm

Owner notes / next steps for this draft:
- @Samira: incorporate SE diagnostic checklist from Ethan (CS-4518) into the article section by 11/10
- @Maya: draft sample exec brief slides and upload by 11/14
- @Jordan: validate finance concession thresholds with Finance and update guardrails by 11/18

Bottom line: this canvas is intentionally pragmatic — short-lived, lightweight, and focused on moving the needle quickly. Use it to create predictable, repeatable outcomes for renewals that are teetering. Keep iterations short and make escalation decisions visible to execs early.

-- end of canvas --
